Subject: Observability integration proposal: Datadog / OpenTelemetry / Grafana

Hi Camila / Jonas —

Thanks again for the intro call today. ObservaTech is seeing strong customer demand for a turnkey observability integration with Redwood that covers three main flows:

- Host-level telemetry into Datadog (metrics + traces) via Datadog Agent
- OpenTelemetry-compatible traces exported to our tracing backend for correlation
- Grafana-ready dashboards that visualize request latency, KV cache hit rates, and per-model token throughput

I attached a short integration_outline.pdf that sketches what we think the integration should include (collector config, expected event volume, dashboard layouts). Our ask: partner with Redwood for a co-built connector and a joint go-to-market (webinar + one-page solution brief).

Can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with your SEs next week? Availability windows: Tue/Wed morning PT or Thu afternoon PT.

Also: we'll need a short SOC2 and encryption-in-transit note for our security review — happy to take the lead collecting any artifacts you can share.

Thanks,

—Daniel

Appreciate the clear outline and the go-to-market idea. We’re excited about working with ObservaTech.

Jonas — looping you in as partner lead. Marissa, can you review the attached outline and flag any API/collector gaps? Priority items from our side: 1) a robust OpenTelemetry ingestion path that preserves Redwood’s per-token metadata, 2) a Datadog-compatible agent config that won’t blow agent memory at scale, and 3) a Grafana dashboard template we can ship with Redwood Dedicated and Private customers.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa & SEs review integration_outline.pdf and drop technical comments by EOD Mon
- Book a 60-min deep dive on Tue 2026-03-03 10:30 AM PT (please confirm)
- Define a mutual action plan for engineering work + co-marketing (we can draft the MAP after the deep dive)

On the SOC2 artifacts — we have a standard security packet and a short export-friendly doc summarizing encryption and audit logs. I’ll surface that after Marissa confirms the technical approach.

Daniel — Tue 10:30 PT work for you?

Best,

Subject: Re: Observability integration proposal: Datadog / OpenTelemetry / Grafana

Thanks — I reviewed the outline and sketched a short tech note (redwood_observability_api.md attached). High-level comments:

- OpenTelemetry: we can emit OTLP over gRPC from our inference gateway; important to include per-request metadata (model_id, sequence_length, cache_hit) as OTLP resource attributes so dashboards can group by model/version.
- Datadog: recommend using the Datadog Agent as a sidecar on Dedicated nodes for metrics and traces. Key config: increase buffer size for high token rates; set trace sampling for low-latency tails to 100% for error traces, 10% for steady-state.
- Grafana: we'll provide a dashboard JSON that includes panels for token/sec, avg latency p50/p95/p99, cost-per-1k-tokens, and cache hit heatmaps.

Open questions:
1) Do partners want raw token logs forwarded (very high volume) or summary aggregates? Suggest aggregates by default and offer a forwarding opt-in for specific customers.
2) For Private deployments, we need to provide an installable collector package and a config guide; I can draft that post-deep-dive.

I attached redwood_observability_api.md with examples (collector snippets, sample Grafana dashboard ids). If that looks good, I’ll prep a draft MAP and an engineering estimate (2 sprints) for the connector.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
